claims.head: Unstoppable force, meet immovable object
claims.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Avalanche are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Stars’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Stars’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Avalanche.

claims.head: In close against from distance
claims.body: The Stars get in close, but the Avalanche mostly shoot from distance. Dallas is one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and Colorado is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Stars to do more of their damage around the net.

notes.text: W. Johnston is out (illness) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. T. Seguin has taken his spot beside M. Rantanen and S. Steel.
M. Duchene is on long-term injured reserve (abdomen injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Z. L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.

COL.head: The Avalanche have a lot going for them
COL.body: Even though Dallas gets Kiviranta back, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Dallas will be without Johnston. The Stars can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.

DAL.head: Not an easy night for the Stars
DAL.body: Even though Dallas gets Kiviranta back, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Dallas will be without Johnston. The Stars’ best way through is a penalty kill that holds up.

story.head: MacKinnon’s favorite opponent
paras: The Avalanche won the first meeting this season, 3-2 in Dallas. The Stars come in at 2-3-1, the Avs at 4-2-0.

It’s strength against strength: the Stars are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Avalanche are one of the best at the penalty kill. The Stars get in close, but the Avalanche mostly shoot from distance.

items.text: Joel Kiviranta faces Colorado for the first time since leaving.
Tyler Seguin has eight goals in six games against Colorado since 2023-24.
Nathan MacKinnon has a point in eleven straight games against Dallas, and 20 points in his last twelve against them.
Last time these two met, there were two fights. For Nathan MacKinnon, it was his second fight this season, after one in the four seasons before.
